Section 1 of 12

If the Creator Is Good, Why Is the World So Broken?

You do not have to look far to see suffering.

Families experience grief. People betray one another. Addiction takes control. Violence destroys lives. Powerful institutions sometimes hide the truth or harm the people they were supposed to protect.

The pain is real.

If the Creator is loving and powerful, why does He allow these things to happen? Did He create evil? Is He responsible for our suffering? Is there a spiritual conflict taking place behind what we can see?

The Bible does not answer every question about every tragedy. It does, however, reveal where evil began, why it continues, and what the Creator is doing to end it.

The Creator Did Not Make Evil

Read Deuteronomy 32:3–4 ↗ and James 1:13–17 ↗.

Everything the Creator does is just and good. There is no cruelty, dishonesty, or evil in His character.

God did not create sin. He did not design abuse, disease, violence, addiction, or death as part of His original plan.

Read Genesis 1:31 ↗.

When God finished creating the world, He called it “very good.” Humanity lived in peace with the Creator, one another, and the natural world.

Something changed after creation.

Evil began with a created being who turned away from the Creator.

Who Was Lucifer?

Before human life existed, God created angels. These powerful spiritual beings served the Creator and lived in His presence.

One of them held a place of great honor. He is often called Lucifer, a name connected with the morning star.

Read Ezekiel 28:12–17 ↗.

This passage speaks directly about an earthly ruler, but its language also points behind that ruler to a greater spiritual rebellion. It describes a being who was created with wisdom and beauty and who was blameless until evil was found in him.

God did not create Lucifer sinful. He created him perfect and gave him freedom.

Lucifer allowed pride to grow within him. Instead of being grateful for what the Creator had given him, he became consumed with his own beauty, position, and importance.

Read Isaiah 14:12–14 ↗.

This passage addresses the proud king of Babylon while also revealing the spirit behind that pride. Lucifer wanted to raise himself above others and take the position that belonged to God.

His heart moved from gratitude to self-exaltation.

How Could Sin Begin in a Perfect Place?

Sin cannot be explained with a good reason. If it had a good reason, it could be excused.

The Bible calls sin “lawlessness.”

Read 1 John 3:4 ↗.

Sin began when Lucifer chose to distrust the Creator and reject His law of love.

God gave angels and humans the freedom to choose because real love cannot be forced. A person may be controlled by fear, but fear cannot create love. A person may be programmed to obey, but programmed obedience is not a relationship.

Freedom made love possible. It also made rebellion possible.

Lucifer used that freedom to turn against the One who gave him life.

What Did Lucifer Say About God?

Lucifer’s rebellion was built on lies about the Creator’s character.

He suggested that God was unfair, controlling, and unworthy of trust. He wanted other angels to believe they would have greater freedom under his leadership.

Read John 8:44 ↗.

Jesus called the devil a liar and the father of lies. He also called him a murderer because his deception produces suffering and death.

Lucifer became Satan, which means adversary or enemy. He became the devil, which means slanderer or accuser.

His main weapon was not physical strength. It was deception.

He attacked trust in the Creator.

A Conflict Began in Heaven

Read Revelation 12:7–9 ↗.

The Bible describes a conflict in heaven. Michael, a name used for Jesus in His role as commander, led the loyal angels. Satan and the angels who followed him fought against them.

Satan was removed from heaven.

Read Revelation 12:4 ↗.

This symbolic passage indicates that many angels joined his rebellion. These fallen angels are now called demons or evil spirits.

Satan is powerful, but he is not equal to the Creator.

He is a created being. He cannot be everywhere. He does not know everything, and his power has limits. His final defeat is certain.

Why Did God Allow the Rebellion to Continue?

The Creator could have destroyed Satan immediately. But the lies Satan told would have remained unanswered.

Other beings might have wondered:

Was Satan telling the truth?

Was God afraid of being questioned?

Does God demand obedience through force?

The Creator chose to let the results of Satan’s way become visible.

God’s way is based on truth, love, freedom, and life. Satan’s way is based on pride, deception, control, and death.

The universe needed to see the difference clearly.

Read 1 Corinthians 4:9 ↗.

The conflict taking place on Earth is being observed by more than humanity. Our world has become part of a much larger struggle over the character and government of God.

The Creator has allowed the conflict to continue for a limited time. When it ends, everyone will understand where rebellion leads.

Read Nahum 1:9 ↗.

God promises that evil will not rise a second time. When He finally removes sin, no unanswered question will remain about its consequences.

How Did the Conflict Reach Earth?

Read Genesis 3:1–6 ↗.

Satan approached Eve through a serpent and repeated the same lie he had used in heaven: the Creator could not be trusted.

He questioned God’s words. He suggested that God was hiding something good from humanity.

God had warned Adam and Eve that disobedience would lead to death. Satan directly contradicted Him:

“You will not surely die.”

The first temptation on Earth was an attack on the Creator’s character and the truthfulness of His Word.

Adam and Eve chose to believe the deceiver. Their decision damaged humanity’s relationship with God and brought sin and death into the world.

Read Romans 5:12 ↗.

Every generation since then has been born into a world affected by that choice.

Where Does Suffering Come From?

Suffering has several causes.

Some suffering comes from our own choices. Some comes from the choices of other people. Some results from living in a world damaged by sin. The Bible also reveals that Satan works to deceive, tempt, accuse, and destroy.

Read 1 Peter 5:8 ↗ and John 10:10 ↗.

This does not mean every illness, accident, anxious thought, or difficult day is a direct attack from an evil spirit. It also does not mean suffering proves that someone has personally done something wrong.

Read John 9:1–3 ↗.

Jesus rejected the belief that one man’s suffering had to be punishment for a specific sin.

We should avoid blaming hurting people or making confident claims about causes we cannot see.

What we can know is that suffering was never the Creator’s original plan. He sees what has happened, He cares about those who hurt, and He is working to end evil forever.

What Are Satan’s Main Strategies?

Satan’s methods still follow the same pattern seen in heaven and Eden.

He lies about the Creator

He wants you to see God as cruel, distant, impossible to please, or uninterested in your life.

Read Genesis 3:1–5 ↗.

He attacks your identity

He may use shame to tell you that you are worthless, unwanted, permanently damaged, or beyond forgiveness.

Read Revelation 12:10 ↗.

Satan is called the accuser. He wants your failures and wounds to become your entire identity.

The Creator says your deepest identity begins with the fact that He made you and wants to restore you.

He makes harmful choices look freeing

Sin often promises freedom before producing bondage.

Read John 8:34–36 ↗.

Jesus offers freedom that does not leave you controlled by an appetite, substance, secret, habit, or another person.

He divides people

Pride, prejudice, greed, resentment, and the desire for control turn people against one another.

Satan benefits whenever we begin treating human beings as enemies instead of people made in God’s image.

He uses religious appearances

Read 2 Corinthians 11:13–15 ↗.

Not everything that appears spiritual comes from the Creator. Satan can use religious language, impressive signs, and respected leaders to spread deception.

Every spiritual claim must be tested by Scripture and the character of Jesus.

People Are Not the Enemy

Read Ephesians 6:10–12 ↗.

The Bible says our deepest struggle is not against flesh and blood. Human beings may make harmful choices, and justice still matters. Yet people themselves are not the ultimate enemy.

Satan wants us to direct hatred toward other people while ignoring the lies, pride, and sin working beneath the surface.

Jesus calls us to resist evil without becoming like the evil we oppose.

He teaches us to stand for truth, protect the vulnerable, seek justice, and refuse hatred.

How Did Jesus Answer Satan’s Accusations?

Jesus came to reveal the truth about the Creator.

His life showed that God is loving, just, patient, and willing to sacrifice Himself for humanity.

At the cross, Satan’s way and God’s way were placed side by side.

Satan inspired betrayal, false accusations, humiliation, violence, and murder.

Jesus responded with truth, forgiveness, courage, and self-giving love.

Read John 12:31–33 ↗ and Colossians 2:14–15 ↗.

At the cross, Jesus exposed Satan’s character and broke his claim over humanity. Through His resurrection, Jesus proved that sin and death will not win.

Satan continues to fight, but he is a defeated enemy whose time is limited.

Where Is the Conflict Happening Today?

The conflict takes place in governments and institutions, but it also reaches into everyday choices.

It appears when you decide whether to forgive or hold onto hatred.

It appears when you choose truth over a convenient lie.

It appears when you decide whether another person’s dignity matters.

It appears when temptation promises relief but leads toward bondage.

It appears when shame tells you to hide from the Creator while the Holy Spirit invites you to return.

The battle often begins in the mind.

Read Romans 12:2 ↗.

The Creator changes us by renewing our thinking. Satan spreads lies. God answers with truth.

How Can You Stand Against the Enemy?

Stay close to Jesus

Read James 4:7–8 ↗.

Submit your life to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee. Your safety comes from the Creator’s power rather than your own strength.

Fill your mind with Scripture

Read Psalm 119:11 ↗ and Matthew 4:1–11 ↗.

When Satan tempted Jesus, Jesus answered with Scripture. Knowing God’s Word helps you recognize lies.

Pray honestly

Read Matthew 6:13 ↗.

Ask the Creator to protect you from evil, expose deception, and give you strength when you are tempted.

Choose what strengthens your mind

What you repeatedly watch, hear, and practice shapes your thinking. Ask whether something is leading you toward truth, self-control, compassion, and Jesus.

Do not chase supernatural experiences

A spiritual experience is not automatically a message from the Creator. Test every claim by Scripture.

Remember that Jesus is stronger

Read 1 John 4:4 ↗.

You do not need to live in fear of Satan or evil spirits. Jesus has already defeated them and will completely remove evil at the end of the conflict.

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. How does knowing where evil began affect the way you see the Creator?
  2. What was Lucifer’s first major problem?
  3. Why does real love require freedom?
  4. What lie did Satan tell Adam and Eve about God?
  5. Which of Satan’s strategies do you recognize most clearly in the world around you?
  6. Is there a lie about your identity that you have been believing?
  7. How does the life of Jesus answer Satan’s accusations about the Creator?
  8. What choice can you make this week to stand on the side of truth, love, and freedom?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside ten quiet minutes on four different days.

Read one passage each time:

  • Day 1: Ezekiel 28:12–17 ↗ and Isaiah 14:12–14 ↗
  • Day 2: Genesis 3:1–15 ↗
  • Day 3: Revelation 12:7–12 ↗
  • Day 4: Ephesians 6:10–18 ↗

After each reading, write down:

  • What does this passage show me about the conflict between good and evil?
  • What lie or strategy do I notice?
  • What truth does the Creator give in response?
  • How can I apply that truth today?

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, thank You for showing me that evil did not begin with You. Help me recognize the lies of the enemy and understand Your true character. Replace the lies I have believed with the truth of Your Word. Protect my mind, guide my choices, and give me strength to resist anything that pulls me away from You. Thank You that Jesus has defeated Satan and that evil will not last forever. Help me stand with You today. Amen.

Remember This

The Creator is completely good.

He did not create sin or suffering.

Evil began when Lucifer chose pride and rebellion.

Satan’s main weapon is deception about the Creator’s character.

Humanity entered the conflict by choosing to distrust God.

Not every tragedy is a direct punishment or spiritual attack.

People are not the ultimate enemy.

Jesus exposed and defeated Satan through His death and resurrection.

The conflict continues for a limited time, but the Creator will end evil forever.
